text.p: Following are the main stories from Slovenia's Wednesday morning newspapers:

- The central bank of Yugoslavia presents evidence at a Nicosia court hearing regarding the freeze of assets of former Yugoslavia deposited in a Yugoslav off-shore bank in Cyprus. The bank is pushing for the freeze to be lifted.
- President of parliament Janez Podobnik is scheduled to meet top-level officials of NATO and the European Union during his first official visit to Brussels this week.

- Parliamentary parties have so far failed to agree on various proposals for a referendum on whether to limit the number of forest areas nationalised after the World War Two to be returned to their previous owners.

- Employees of troulbed bicycle maker Rog said on Tuesday they would end a strike that lasted over a week, after the Ministry of Economic Affairs said if would assign a special financial consultant to the company for the next six months.
- On Tuesday a six-day international Alpe-Adria fair for home equipment and gardening tools started in Ljubljana.
- Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi is due to meet his counterpart Janez Drnovsek when he visits Ljubljana next Tuesday.

- An explosion on Tuesday in a factory of drug producer Lek in the eastern city of Lendava was caused by a fault in a machine. The explosion wounded one person and caused 27 million tolars ($175,000) of damage.
- Slovenian banks said they would prepare a custodian account scheme for international portfolio investors next week.
- Petrol trading company Petrol said it expected to pay a dividend of 700 tolars ($4.5) per share this year. This will be the first dividend paid by the recenty privatised company.
